error.signature: AI tells a newcomer that having a BSN or legal EU residence guarantees a Dutch bank will open a basic payment account for them

verdict.summary: Everyone lawfully residing in the EU has a statutory right to a 'basisbetaalrekening' (basic payment account) under the Wft, implementing the EU Payment Accounts Directive - Kifid confirms 'Iedereen die rechtmatig in de Europese Unie verblijft... Er bestaat daarom een wettelijk recht op een basisbetaalrekening.' But the right has statutory limits (Wft art. 4:71g): a bank must refuse if it cannot meet Wwft anti-money-laundering duties, and may refuse if the applicant cannot show a genuine need ('werkelijk belang') for a Dutch account, already holds or is applying for an NL-IBAN account, was convicted of fraud/forgery/money-laundering-type offenses within 8 years, or had a basic account terminated for intentional criminal misuse within the last 2 years. Legal residence or a BSN alone does not override these grounds.

dead_ends.action: Tell a newcomer that once they have a BSN and are lawfully resident in the EU, a Dutch bank must open a basic payment account for them, no further questions asked
dead_ends.why_fails: Rijksoverheid.nl and Kifid both confirm the statutory right exists but is not unconditional. Kifid states: 'er kan een reden zijn waarom de bank u zo'n basisbetaalrekening mag of moet weigeren, een zogenoemde weigeringsgrond' (there can be a reason the bank is permitted or required to refuse, a so-called ground for refusal). The bank must refuse if it cannot comply with Wwft anti-money-laundering checks, and may refuse if you cannot demonstrate a genuine need for a Dutch account, already hold or are applying for one elsewhere in NL, or have a disqualifying conviction or account-misuse history within the statutory lookback windows.
dead_ends.condition: Applying for a basisbetaalrekening as a legally-resident foreigner
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the 'legal right to a bank account' works like an unconditional entitlement once you're a legal resident, rather than a default right the bank can still lawfully refuse on specific grounds.

dead_ends.action: Assume the refusal grounds are vague bank discretion rather than specific statutory tests
dead_ends.why_fails: Basisbankrekening.nl (the Dutch Banking Association's own covenant site) cites the exact statutory basis: Wft article 4:71g lists refusal grounds including failing Wwft compliance, lacking 'werkelijk belang' (genuine need) for an NL account, already holding or applying for one, a conviction within 8 years for offenses like 'valsheid in geschrifte... oplichting... witwassen' (forgery, fraud, money laundering), or a prior basic account terminated within 2 years for intentional criminal use - these are specific, enumerated tests, not open-ended discretion.
dead_ends.condition: Understanding why a specific application was refused

workarounds.action: If you don't already hold or can't get a regular account, apply for a basisbetaalrekening directly with a Dutch bank and be ready to document your 'werkelijk belang' (genuine need) for a Dutch account - e.g. proof of residence, employment, or study in the Netherlands
workarounds.how: Bring ID, BSN, and documentation of your connection to the Netherlands (residence permit, employment contract, enrollment letter); this is the evidence banks use to assess the statutory 'genuine need' test.
workarounds.condition: First-time applicant with no other NL bank account

workarounds.action: If refused, first file a written complaint with the bank itself, then escalate to Kifid (the statutory financial-services complaints institute) if unresolved
workarounds.condition: Application refused without a valid statutory ground
workarounds.tradeoff: Complaint resolution through Kifid takes time and is not guaranteed to succeed if a valid refusal ground applies.
